# requireNonScalar

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not a scalar.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonScalar() — Returns the value after checking that it is not a scalar. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonScalar<T>(
  value: T | string | number | boolean | symbol | bigint,
  message: string = "Expected a non-scalar value."
): T;
```

A primitive that carries a single value: string, number, boolean, symbol or bigint. `null` and `undefined` are primitives too, but they carry no value and do not qualify.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                 | Type                                                   | Description                                                   |
| :-------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                   | `T \| string \| number \| boolean \| symbol \| bigint` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-scalar value."` | `string`                                               | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with a scalar excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition              |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is a scalar. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonScalar({}); // => {}
requireNonScalar([]); // => []
requireNonScalar("abc"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonScalar(1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
